title: What is query optimization and how do you read an execution plan?
description: Learn to analyze and optimize SQL Server query performance.

data.text: **Question:** What is query optimization and how do you read an execution plan?
Query optimization involves analyzing and improving SQL query performance. The execution plan shows how SQL Server executes a query, including indexes used, join algorithms, and estimated costs.

**Execution Plan Components:**
- **Clustered Index Scan/Seek:** Table access method
- **Key Lookup:** Additional lookups for non-indexed columns
- **Nested Loops:** Join algorithm for small datasets
- **Hash Match:** Join algorithm for large datasets
- **Merge Join:** Join algorithm for sorted data

**Optimization Techniques:**
- Use appropriate indexes
- Avoid SELECT *
- Use WHERE clauses effectively
- Avoid functions in WHERE clauses
- Use JOINs instead of subqueries

data.title: Execution Plan Analysis
data.code:
-- Generate execution plan
SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON;
GO
SELECT * FROM Orders 
WHERE CustomerId = 123;
GO
SET SHOWPLAN_XML OFF;

-- Look for:
-- - Index Seek (good) vs Index Scan (bad)
-- - Key Lookups (consider covering index)
-- - Table Scans (missing indexes)

data.text: Interviewers want to assess ability to diagnose query performance issues and apply optimization techniques.

items: How do you identify missing indexes?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Execution plans show query execution strategy
Index Seek is better than Index Scan
Avoid Key Lookups with covering indexes
Use DMVs to find missing indexes
data.takeaway: Always analyze execution plans for slow queries and optimize based on actual execution behavior.
